# Child Activation Functions

A callable function library for preparing child documents with independently declared party roles, while retaining a legacy construction method that reuses parent role names. Preparation returns child content; it does not initialize the child, obtain acceptance or grant timeline access. Reads from `/activation` concern the document executing the functions. Paths changed inside the `child` argument concern the returned child.

## Explicit child preparation

`bindChild(child, mapping)` calls `prepareChild(child, mapping, suppliedRoles)` with `suppliedRoles=[]`.

`prepareChild` requires an uninitialized child with the exact Activation Clause type at `/clauses/activation/type`. It rejects an existing `/contracts/initialized` with `CHILD_ALREADY_INITIALIZED`, and a missing or different activation type with `CHILD_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED`.

The child's `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties` supplies its role declarations; the executing document's `/activation/parties` supplies the configuring parties. Both rosters must be nonempty objects, and `mapping` must be an object. Each mapping key names a declared child role. Its value is either a parent role name or an explicit Party value. There is no implicit mapping by matching role names.

Each mapped Party must satisfy the child's declaration and have a `lead/channel` plus a nonempty `readerKeys` list of distinct, nonempty text values. Every parent party's main identity must appear in the resolved child roster: identity matching requires the exact lead channel and the same primary reader-key set, regardless of key order. Matching labels alone is insufficient. Child role names must be nonempty and contain none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Unknown roles, missing mappings, invalid parties and missing parent identities are rejected.

`suppliedRoles` permits explicitly listed child roles to remain unmapped, retaining their declarations. Each such role must exist in the declarations and must not also occur in `mapping`. This function does not automatically resolve these retained declarations. The inherited `mapParties` helper exposes the same mapping rules with no supplied-role exceptions.

Preparation preserves the child's existing `accessPaths`, treating an omitted list as empty. It appends references to every parent access document under `/timelineAccess/configurerN`, where numbering starts at the existing child path-list length. An occupied target causes `CHILD_ACCESS_PATH_CONFLICT`, even if its content matches. Other activation parameters remain unchanged.

For resolved entries containing `lead/channel`, preparation installs the lead transport under `/contracts/<role>` and additional representative transports under `/contracts/<role>__<representative>`. An identical existing channel is accepted; a different one causes `CHILD_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. Copying these references and channels does not establish valid access or participant consent.

## Legacy same-role construction

`activateChild(child, frozen, readerNames, roles)` returns `child` unchanged when the executing document has no `/activation`. Otherwise, `roles=[]` selects every parent party; a nonempty list selects only those parent roles. `readerNames` selects named entries from `/activation/readers`; an empty list copies no extra reader groups. Unknown selections fail with `CHILD_PARTY_NOT_IN_PARENT` or `CHILD_READER_NOT_IN_PARENT`.

This function replaces the child's `timelineAccess` map with references named `grant0`, `grant1`, and so on, covering all parent `accessPaths`. It replaces the activation clause with an Activation Clause, retaining existing parameters except for `parties`, `readers`, `accessPaths` and the supplied Boolean `frozen`. Existing `required` is retained; if absent, it is explicitly set to `[]`. This matters because ordinary Activation planning defaults an absent `required` to all roster roles, whereas an explicit empty list requires no party approvals.

Legacy construction writes selected lead and representative channels without the initialized-child or collision checks used by `prepareChild`.

## Inherited activation and access behavior

The library inherits Activation Functions and their supporting access, mapping and amendment helpers. It declares no automatic trigger itself. An Activation Clause installs handlers that refresh activation after clause initialization and relevant embedded access updates.

Activation maintains separate acceptance and access conditions. `approved` records party-lead acceptance; `required` identifies the approvals needed. `termsAccepted` also requires the document's negotiated fields to match their recorded agreed values. `accessReady` and `functional` express the access check. `active` requires both conditions and a document that is not `closed`.

The computed `status` distinguishes `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` after prior activation, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` when access is ready but acceptance or agreed-field consistency is missing, `ACTIVE`, and `CLOSED`. `everActivated` remains true after activation even if access is later lost. `commitState` emits first-activation and access suspension/restoration events on the corresponding transitions. Missing persisted state is not proof of any of these outcomes. Separately, the compatibility helpers `businessReady` and `requireActive` bypass activation checks when `/activation` is absent.

`approve` requires exact-document review, invocation through a party's lead channel, the current `revision`, and valid participant access. Negotiation-enabled approval requires `termsRef`; any supplied reference must match the current terms. A new approval is recorded and activation is reevaluated; an already recorded approval returns successfully without another acceptance event. Approval by one party does not establish overall activation.

`updateParty` also requires exact-document review and a party-lead channel. Omitted `input.party` targets the invoking party. Existing parties cannot be managed through another party's lead. Adding a party requires `allowNewParties`; `frozen` blocks management. Replacement data must contain `lead/channel`, valid representative names and sufficient access. A successful update installs the resulting contracts, clears approvals, increments activation `revision`, and adds a newly created role to `required`.

`admitApprovedParties` instead checks the expected activation revision, an unfrozen roster and a nonempty configured `admission.approvers` policy. Existing roles must retain their main identity; new roles are added only with sufficient access and without contract-name conflicts. This helper does not itself collect admission approvals, and it does not append admitted roles to `required`. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster returns `acceptedNew` after recording its changes.

`requestPartyAddition` handles a Party Addition Requested event. It ignores stale revisions and already recorded admission references, validates supplied access documents and records pending additions. Same-revision pending additions participate in activation's access check before admission completes. Where existing parties need broader access coverage, it emits Party Access Update Requested events for their transports. These are requests, not granted permissions or consent.

Access checks derive reader groups from `readers`, each party's `readerKeys`, and each additional representative's `readerKeys`. External Channel transports bypass the private-timeline check. Other transports must be Timeline Channels. For each such transport, one same-provider Timeline Access document must include the exact timeline and at least one key from every reader group. These helpers do not combine partial key coverage across several documents for one transport. Operation authority remains separate from read access; listing a representative does not authorize every party operation.

`installTimelineAccess` takes `input.basePath` and between one and sixteen `input.documents`. It requires native Timeline Access documents with initialization evidence, a provider checkpoint and the expected provider/update executable contracts. It deduplicates by original document identity, returning `duplicate` if nothing is added. Otherwise it stores references, registers access-update refresh channels, extends `activation.accessPaths` and returns `acceptedNew`. Permission changes remain provider-owned.

## Terms and amendment helpers

`initializeTerms` preserves existing terms or records the configured scalar negotiation fields and a content-based terms reference. New terms initialize `termsRevision` and negotiation `revision` to 1, with negotiation `editable=true`. Changing parties or `required` changes the terms identity, closes a pending proposal with `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation is enabled.

Configured negotiation distinguishes the current `terms.ref` from a pending proposal's `baseTermsRef`, `termsRef`, `id` and `proposer`. Proposed terms must still be based on the current terms when approved. Selecting proposed terms requires their `proposalId`; selecting current terms must omit it. A fully approved proposal is applied and closes editing. Recorded proposal outcomes distinguish `APPLIED`, `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `SUPERSEDED` and `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`; a proposal record alone is not agreement.

The inherited generic amendment helpers use caller-supplied `bindings.state`, `bindings.editable`, `parameters.paths` and `parameters.approvers`. `recordAmendmentProposal` checks the expected revision, an allowed path, editability and a nonempty unused `proposalId` containing neither `/` nor `~`. Repeating the same pending identifier requires identical path, replacement and revision. `preservePending=true` prevents replacing a different pending proposal.

`approveAmendmentProposal` requires an approver channel. Closed proposals and repeated approvals return `duplicate`; new approvals require the matching pending proposal and editable terms. Only when every configured approver has approved does it replace the target value, record completion in history, increment the amendment revision, clear the proposal and emit Amendment Applied. An accepted individual approval can therefore leave the proposal pending.
